And finally, I made some test code to get myself familiarize.

I understand that the fundamental part is to identify which parts can be parallelized and be careful about dependencies.

If the parallel processes are independent, then we can simply use `omp parallel for`. 

```cpp
#pragma omp parallel for
for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
    a[i] = b[i] + c[i];
}
```

But if the parallel processes are treating one global variable, such as summing it up. We need to be careful. we can use `reduction` to ensure the summing is happening one by one.

```c
int sum = 0;
#pragma omp parallel for reduction(+:sum)
for (int i = 1; i <= max; i++) {
	sum = sum + i;
}
```

Function parallelism is usually more complex because it involves dependencies. We can use `omp single` to ensure that each task is created only once, and `omp task` to allow the tasks to run in parallel. So, without `single`, each thread may create its own `foo`, `bar`, and `baz` tasks, causing them to run multiple times. Without `task`, `foo`, `bar`, and `baz` are executed sequentially by a single thread.

```c
#pragma omp parallel
{
    #pragma omp single
    {
        #pragma omp task
        foo();
        #pragma omp task
        bar();
        #pragma omp task
        baz();
    }
}
```

And these are important for controlling and evaluating the processes. 

```c
// omp_get_num_threads()
// omp_set_num_threads()
// omp_get_thread_num()
// omp_get_wtime()

#include <stdio.h>
#include <omp.h>

int main(void)
{
    omp_set_num_threads(4);
    double start = omp_get_wtime();
    #pragma omp parallel
    {
        int id = omp_get_thread_num();
        int num_threads = omp_get_num_threads();
        printf("Hello from thread %d of %d\n",
               id, num_threads);
    }
    double end = omp_get_wtime();
    printf("Execution time: %f seconds\n", end - start);
    return 0;
}
```

## Exercise 2.2

The intuition I got from `omp_mm.c` sample code is, in matrix multiplication, each row of the result is independent.
In the implementation, `schedule (static, chunk)` assings fixed 10 chunks of parallel processing, which is 10 rows not one by one though.  

And I believe, even each cell of the result should be independent. So I made a custom code `omp_mm_cell.c`.

```c
// ORIGINAL CODE
// #pragma omp for schedule (static, chunk)
// for (i=0; i<NRA; i++)
//   {
//   printf("Thread=%d did row=%d\n",tid,i);
//   for(j=0; j<NCB; j++)
//     for (k=0; k<NCA; k++)
//       c[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
//   }
// /*** End of parallel region ***/

// NEW CODE CELL UNIT PARALLELIZATION.
#pragma omp for collapse(2) schedule(static, chunk)
for (i = 0; i < NRA; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j < NCB; j++) {

        printf("Thread=%d did cell=(%d,%d)\n", tid, i, j);

        for (k = 0; k < NCA; k++)
            c[i][j] += a[i][k] * b[k][j];
    }
}
```

By adding `omp_get_wtime()`, I measured each strategy and compared them by changing the number of threads with `omp_set_num_threads()`.
One warm-up run and 5 measurement runnings, and reporting the median.

```{python}
import subprocess

subprocess.run(["gcc", "-fopenmp", "omp_mm.c", "-o", "mm"], check=True)
subprocess.run(["gcc", "-fopenmp", "omp_mm_cell.c", "-o", "mm_cell"], check=True)

for threads in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64]:
    print("Threads:", threads)
    for name, program in [("Row", "./mm"), ("Cell", "./mm_cell")]:
        result = subprocess.run(
            [program, str(threads)], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
        )
        median_time = next(
            line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if "Median elapsed time" in line
        )
        print(name, "strategy:", median_time)
```

The result is interesting. I interpret it that the overhead of coordination (in the cell strategy, handling much more parallel processings) is higher. 

## Exercise 2.3

### Task 2.3.1
By adding `omp_get_wtime()`, I measured the elapsed time of the naive serial and recursive serial versions. Here is the result.

```{python}
import subprocess

subprocess.run(["g++", "-fopenmp", "matmul_recur.cpp", "-o", "matmul_recur"], check=True)

for size in [10, 100, 500, 1000]:
    print("Matrix dimensions:", size, size, size)
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["./matmul_recur", str(size), str(size), str(size)],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    print(result.stdout)
    if size == 1000:
        line = next(line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if "T recursive median" in line)
        serial_recursive_median = float(line.split()[4])
```

I was surprised that the recurrsive is faster.
I actually didn't understand why, but genAI suggested reasonable hypothesis, this is because of cache efficiency.
I tried to evaluate it by using 'perf' counter with L1 cache behavior, but unfortunately I was not allowed to install these in the parcomp computer.

### Task 2.3.2
By thinking which part can be independent in the recursive approach, These C00, C01, C10, C11 these 4 processes are independent.
So, in essense by setting these 2 functions as one task,
```c
#pragma omp task
{
    // C00 += A00 * B00
		matmultrec(mf, mf+(ml-mf)/2, nf, nf+(nl-nf)/2, pf, pf+(pl-pf)/2, A, B, C);
    // C00 += A01 * B10
        matmultrec(mf, mf+(ml-mf)/2, nf, nf+(nl-nf)/2, pf+(pl-pf)/2, pl, A, B, C);
}
```

I compared $T_{recursive,1}$ with $T_{recursive,p}$ using 1, 2, 4, and 8 threads.

```{python}
import os
import subprocess

subprocess.run(
    ["g++", "-fopenmp", "matmul_recur_parallel.cpp", "-o", "matmul_recur_parallel"],
    check=True,
)

print("T recursive,1 median:", serial_recursive_median, "seconds")
for threads in [1, 2, 4, 8]:
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["OMP_NUM_THREADS"] = str(threads)
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["./matmul_recur_parallel"],
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    line = next(line for line in result.stdout.splitlines() if "T recursive median" in line)
    parallel_recursive_median = float(line.split()[4])
    print("Threads:", threads)
    print("T recursive,p median:", parallel_recursive_median, "seconds")
    print("T recursive,1 / T recursive,p:", serial_recursive_median / parallel_recursive_median)
```
